top_choice_rationale: P001 credits Katori and Ye with the invention of the optical lattice clock, a distinct mechanism (magic-wavelength trapping cancels the lattice light shift, allowing many atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime) with demonstrated fractional uncertainty near 1e-18 reproduced independently with Sr, Yb and Hg. That is a mature, experimentally verified invention that fits the discovery-or-invention criterion, and a two-name allocation with a citation naming magic-wavelength trapping keeps the scope bounded. The novelty margin over the 2005 and 2012 prizes and the unverified priority record are real but do not outweigh this; an award is preferred to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no documented tie to Katori, Ye or optical clocks. Her electron-microscopy field is unrelated to optical clocks, and the only noted connection is that Goran Johansson is also at Chalmers.
